the microarchitecture level interconnect model is a powerful tool that can help designers to understand the power and performance of a given floorplan and to optimize the microarchitecture for a given floorplan.
microarchitecture-level power estimation and layout optimization should be considered together to improve both power efficiency (Watt/IPC) and throughput (IPC).

microarchitecture-level interconnection modeling considering layout optimization can improve both power and throughput at the early design stages.
interconnects should be considered in the microarchitecture-level modeling, and the layout optimization for interconnects should consider the performance of microarchitecture.

the proposed microarchitecture-level modeling of interconnect power and performance is accurate, and the proposed microarchitecture and layout co-optimization can improve both power efficiency as well as throughput.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conventional microarchitecture-level interconnection modeling is not accurate and may lead to design errors.
the conventional design flow is not sufficient for the next generation of processors and that coupled microarchitecture and floorplan optimization is necessary to maximize throughput.
